independent_qualification: Sequential local byte observations require stable noncooperating byte custody and prove no atomic snapshot or future copied/upload bytes.

Authentic original capture/transfer/extent metadata, application subset safety/consistency and restored acceptance, exact current permissions, command custody and qualified dispatch remain integration-owned.
No provider calls, paid effects, upload/load/start permit, current Active fence, automatic receipt, terminal proof or fence/reference-release/prune admission is created.
local_effects: Held source download journal borrows source layout; returned view also borrows restore layout/plans/requirement. Exact retained requirement/plans/manifest/journal are admitted before and after fresh no-follow checks of every original source tree, including source artifacts outside a restore subset.

The manifest owner admits reads under an already-held download journal without reacquiring its lock, retaining the unchanged original journal check and expected full digest. Existing standalone manifest replay remains record-only.
No data records, spending, fence obligations or references are changed. Missing/unsafe/changed evidence and bytes, contention or replaced custody return typed failures without repair or reset.
original_binding: Exact full original restore/source plan hashes and original requirement digest; same declared network/release and existing selected restore IDs contained in the source selection.

Opt-in local source binding requires source_artifacts equal the existing complete canonical DownloadJournalRecord digest. Generic integration artifact digests are not reinterpreted or rejected by their existing owners.

Manifest requires exact full original source intent, complete selected-source coverage and every entry Durable with its retained checksum. Exact snapshot tokens, metadata and derived paths are reused, never rebound.
Selected restore artifact views borrow the original complete durable source declarations in canonical principal order. Source and restore callers can differ; current permissions remain separate.
recovery: Drop/reopen retains exact original requirement/manifest/journal and pending spent attempts. Fresh verification is explicitly repeated only when requested; ordinary manifest replay and terminal replay perform no artifact/provider verification.
